newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech shares tumble before holiday weekend.
newsitem.headline: Czech shares tumble before holiday weekend.

text.p: Czech shares tumbled on Friday pulling the PX50 index and especially the major issue dominated RPIX index sharply lower.
The PX50 lost 10.5 points to 521.3 while the RPIX fell 32 points to 1,052.

Traders said the Czech equity market was suffering from long standing structural problems and nervousness before mid-November's Senatorial elections but they were at a loss to explain why Friday should have seen such heavy losses.
"Today it could be because of lower volumes before the national holiday (on Monday). Otherwise I can think of no reason for it to happen specially now," said Jeff Ocenasek of Atlantik Financni Trhy.

Ocenasek said that international investors, particularly, were showing scant ineterest in the Czech market and had been put off by the absence of a strong regulatory framework and inadequate legislation protecting minority shareholders.
Major issues, in which foreigners trade heavily, took the brunt of the selling pressure.
Komercni Banka fell 70 crowns to 2,150, SPT Telecom lost 55 crowns to 2,995, CEZ dropped 47 crowns to 961 and Ceska Sporitelna was off 13 crowns to 330.
Collectively, the above four shares account for around half the PX50's total capitalisation and therefore strongly influence the direction of the index.
